business_problem: Virta needed to replace a monolithic data architecture that could not keep pace with millions of EV charging messages, leading to operational blockages, slow customer updates, and a development team distracted by running Kafka at scale.
solution_summary: Virta made Confluent Cloud the real-time backbone of its cloud-based EV charging platform so teams could process charging-station events and customer-facing updates without the bottlenecks of its earlier architecture. The managed service replaced self-operated Kafka and now handles high-volume telemetry and operational messages while Schema Registry and developer tooling make it easier for teams to build new event-driven services securely. Because the platform scales elastically with demand, Virta can process surges automatically instead of planning and rebalancing clusters by hand. The streaming layer feeds app features, new charging-point rollouts, and real-time operational visibility, including sub-second configuration updates and rapid outage awareness. By moving the data backbone to Confluent, Virta's engineers shifted their time from infrastructure work to launching new features and expanding the platform into additional markets.

solution_components.name: Confluent Cloud
solution_components.role: Runs Virta's real-time streaming backbone for EV charging and customer-experience data.

solution_components.name: Schema Registry
solution_components.role: Provides a secure common language for developers creating new event-driven services.

data_flow: Charging-station and application events stream into Confluent Cloud, where they are distributed to downstream services that update customer apps, support new charge-point launches, and surface real-time operational information such as station status and configuration changes.
business_outcome: Virta sped up feature and market expansion, processed far more charging events without manual scaling, and improved customer responsiveness by reflecting station changes in under a second.
architecture_clues: Virta uses the managed streaming platform as the backbone of a new cloud-based platform rather than as a sidecar to the old monolith.
Developer tooling includes Schema Registry and pre-built APIs for internal teams.
The company is considering future integration with Snowflake's AI data cloud, but the current backbone is Confluent Cloud.
